outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Low-Bit Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter sets the stage by exploring the current landscape of Large Language Model (LLM) development. It highlights the trade-offs between model performance, computational efficiency, and environmental impact. Students will learn why standard 16-bit floating-point models face bottlenecks in memory bandwidth and energy consumption, introducing the concept of quantization as a solution.
subtopics: The Rise of LLMs and Computational Bottlenecks
Understanding Quantization: Post-Training vs. Training from Scratch
Limitations of Existing Low-Precision Methods (FP8, INT4)
Motivation for Moving to Binary/Ternary Architectures

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Introducing BitNet b1.58 – Architecture and Core Concepts
outline.description: A deep dive into the central innovation of the paper: BitNet b1.58. This chapter explains how replacing dense float layers with ternary sparse representations transforms the neural network structure without sacrificing expressiveness.
subtopics: Decoding '1.58 Bits': Why Not Purely Binary?
The Role of Zero: Feature Filtering and Sparsity
Architectural Overhaul: Replacing nn.Linear with BitLinear

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Implementation Details – From Theory to Code
outline.description: Technical guide for implementing BitNet b1.58. This section breaks down the mathematical machinery behind quantizing weights and activations, ensuring students understand exactly how continuous gradients map to discrete integers during backpropagation.
subtopics: [Equation Analysis] The AbsMean Quantization Function Explained
(Step-by-step Derivatives): Differentiable Relaxation via Straight-Through Estimator Logic
(Clarification Note]: Scaling Activations per Token [-Qb, Qb]
.Adopting Modern Transformers: LLaMA-Alike Components (RMSNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU)
